author_comment.body: Working on this in #31985. ## Current understanding of the behavior - **Current behavior:** when Zulip's prettified channel link syntax is pasted into the URL placeholder of ordinary Markdown hyperlink syntax — e.g. `[my link](#**Denmark**)` — the outer link is silently destroyed. Instead of one `my link`, the channel syntax is turned into its own `` element *inside* the parentheses, so the surrounding `[label](...)` syntax never gets a chance to become a link. - **Expected behavior:** `[my link](#**Denmark**)` should render as a single normal hyperlink whose label is `my link` and whose href is the resolved narrow URL: `my link`. This affects all three prettified variants: | Input | Expected href | | --- | --- | | `[label](#**Denmark**)` | `/#narrow/channel/9-Denmark` | | `[label](#**Denmark>some topic**)` | `/#narrow/channel/9-Denmark/topic/some.20topic` | | `[label](#**Denmark>danish@123**)` | `/#narrow/channel/9-Denmark/topic/danish/near/123` | ## What I did to replicate and learn about the issue - Reproduced by sending `[my link](#**Denmark**)` in a message and inspecting the rendered HTML — the anchor's href is not the narrow URL, and there is a nested `` where the URL should be. - Traced this to Zulip's inline-processor registration in `zerver/lib/markdown/__init__.py`. The relevant priorities are: ``` stream_topic_message 89 StreamTopicMessagePattern topic 87 StreamTopicPattern stream 85 StreamPattern link 60 LinkInlineProcessor <-- generic [label](url) ``` Because all three prettified-link processors run at a *higher* priority than Python-Markdown's generic `LinkInlineProcessor`, they consume the `#**Denmark**` text and emit an `` element before the outer `[label](...)` syntax is ever considered. - Checked why the syntax matches at all inside the parentheses. `BEFORE_LINK_PRODUCING_MENTION_ALLOWED_REGEX` in `zerver/lib/mention.py` is `(?` element. 3. The consumed span is replaced by plain URL text, so the lower-priority `LinkInlineProcessor` (priority 60) then sees a well-formed `[label](/#narrow/channel/...)` and renders the outer link correctly.
